- 2026-07-09 · Part 2 §4/§8.1 (P1.8b) · **squat, jump_squat, chair_squat all ship `rep.metric: "knee_L"` (+`knee_R` fallback)** — the legacy rep_counter joint (`left_knee`, right fallback; rep_counter.py:15,162-164). RESOLVES the FOOTNOTE 2 / rep-metric SPEC GAP: measured `knee_avg` vs `knee_L` on all 9 goldens — `knee_avg` matches on the 3 squat clips but UNDERCOUNTS chair (Chair_Squat_goodform_sideview1 2→1) and jump (jump_squat_goodform_sideview2 2→0), because with `knee_avg` the bilateral-gate "other knee" flips (session.ts:207) and the mean absorbs the deeper leg. `knee_L` is the faithful port and keeps all 9 green. `squat.json` v6 supersedes `squat.v5.json`'s illustrative `knee_avg`; v5 stays as the P1.7 worked-example fixture. **squat.json also DROPS the worked example's `minRepMs: 900` and `maxRepMs: 12000` — neither is ported** (legacy `_min_rep_interval`=0.45s→450 only; rep_counter.py:148, and the inventory flags 900 as squat.v5-only and maxRepMs as having no legacy source, lines 39/176-178). `minRepMs:900` is behaviourally live — `max(450, minRepMs)` (fsm.ts:96) would double the rep-interval floor with no port basis, so it's removed; the ported 450 engine floor stands. (T3 P1.8b finding V1/V2.)
- 2026-07-09 · Part 2 §7.6 (P1.8b) · traces.replay drives all 9 parity traces through COMPILED §4 definitions (test/definitions/{squat,jump_squat,chair_squat}.json), lint-gated before replay; hand-built `parity-configs.ts` retired; `scripts/fsm-parity-debug.ts` repointed to compiled defs. reps-exact + scoreRange green 9/9.
- 2026-07-09 · Part 2 §3.8 (P1.8b) · **Only squat is scored faithfully today.** jump depth/trunk/valgus are per-frame gated on `is_loading`/`currently_airborne`/`just_landed` (form_analyzer.py:441-504) and chair depth is target-relative (`full_at=target+10`, form_analyzer.py:123-159) — neither is expressible in the scoring model (fixed-number curve x, per-rep aggregates, no airborne state). jump & chair ship exact COUNTING + expressible faults (jump-local valgus −0.15/−0.25; chair valgus −0.15/−0.30) + a **documented INTERIM/placeholder depth scorer**, gated on reps+scoreRange only. The interim curve *numbers* ARE §8.1-traceable — jump `[[90,100],[140,40]]` from §D (form_analyzer.py:450 anchor 90/span 60, :445 loading-fault 40, LOADING_DEPTH_MIN 140); chair `[[110,100],[125,40],[155,0]]` from §C's fallback-target path (CHAIR_FALLBACK_TARGET 100 +TOLERANCE 10, +SHALLOW_MARGIN 25, STANDING 155) — but they are INTERIM because the per-frame airborne gating (jump) and calibrated-target anchoring (chair) that Python applies around them cannot be reproduced, so they must NOT be read as faithful per-rep scorers. Chair trunk-lean and jump trunk-lean are `(trunk − shin)` relative comparisons the DSL cannot express (no binary subtraction) → deferred with the same template work. See the two SPEC GAPs below. (T3 P1.8b finding V3.)

- 2026-07-09 · Part 2 §7.6/§1.3 I5 (P1.9) · **Perf gate armed.** test/perf.test.ts replays a real golden looped to 9000 frames (10 min @15fps) through the real squat engine. Measured on the dev box: **p50 ≈ 0.011 ms, p95 ≈ 0.03 ms** — ~100× under budget. INTERPRETATION (SPEC GAP resolution): §7.6's "≤3 ms scaled to the CI baseline machine" is enforced here as a **regression TRIPWIRE** (`p95 ≤ 3 ms` on CI); the true ≤3 ms *mid-Android (₹12k)* device budget (I5) is verified at the **P5 §3.2 mobile spike** on real hardware (a dev/CI box is faster than mid-Android, so CI-pass is necessary, not sufficient). Consistent with the playbook's "a model-estimated frame rate is not a result" stance.
- 2026-07-09 · Part 2 §7.6/I5 (P1.9) · **Heap-flat gate.** Asserts heap delta over the 9000-frame run. `vitest.config.ts` runs the suite in forks with `--expose-gc`, so the **STRICT bound (<5 MB, forced GC) is the one CI actually enforces** — reproducibly **≈ −25.8 MB** (GC reclaims all per-frame garbage). The loose **<40 MB** path is only a fallback for a runner without `--expose-gc`; its natural-GC delta is **NOISY (observed roughly −5 to +25 MB across back-to-back runs)** and must NOT be read as a stable figure — it exists to avoid flaking, not to catch leaks. (T3 P1.9: the loose path alone was leak-permeable; strict is now armed.) **The R5.5 ring-buffer refactor was NOT needed** — per-frame allocations are fully reclaimed under forced GC; that deferral is closed as "measured, no action required at P1.9," kept honest by the strict gate going forward.
- 2026-07-09 · Part 2 §7.6/§3.6 (P1.9) · **Fuzz pass green.** test/fuzz.test.ts drives seeded (mulberry32) NaN / dropout-burst / 8–40 fps jitter on the squat/chair/jump good goldens (40 seeds × 4 variants each) + a recovery case. All three invariants hold: no throw (I6), rep count never exceeds the clean baseline, counting recovers after a full dropout. **Confirms the 2026-07-08 debounce decision**: raw frame-count debounce (3 down/2 up) does NOT let fps jitter increase counts — no time-normalization change needed.

- 2026-07-10 · Part 2 §2.4 / Part 4 §3.5 (P1.10d T3) · **Sync contract tightened with DDL-derived bounds:** setIndex/reps ≤ 32767 (smallint), durationMs/holdMs/tempoMsAvg/definitionVersion/defsVersion ≤ 2147483647 (int4), sets[] non-empty (the P1.10c all-log-only decision, now enforced server-side too), sets[] ≤ 32767 (sets_count smallint), duplicate setIndex rejected (it would silently drop rows under the §3.5 ON CONFLICT upsert and desync the server-derived aggregates). ## Pending (SPEC GAPs raised, awaiting Kd)

- **SPEC GAP (P1.8b→P4): jump-squat airborne-state scoring/faults.** Stiff-landing, loading-depth window, just-landed landing score, and `(trunk−shin)` relative lean all need per-frame airborne gating (hip_elevation crossing 0.15, landing window `0<elev<0.30`) that the current scoring/fault template cannot express. The P1.8b jump definition ships counting + an interim depth curve only; the airborne apparatus is deferred to the P4 jump task with a template/DSL extension. (R5.6: template gap, NOT an engine special-case.)
- **SPEC GAP (P1.8b→P4): chair adaptive depth scoring.** The legacy chair depth curve is anchored to the C2 `target` (full credit at `target+10`, shallow at `target+25`); the scoring schema's curve x-values are fixed numbers (only the fault DSL has `target+N`). Chair depth ships an interim fixed-fallback-target curve; target-relative score curves are deferred to the P4 template work. (Independent of the C2-formula SPEC GAP below — even the §3.5 formula's target can't be threaded into a score curve today.)
- **SPEC GAP (P1.8b gate debt (a) RECLASSIFIED — needs a decision):** the "±3-vs-Python per-rep score" assertion has **no defined extraction rule**. Python emits a per-FRAME `form_score`; the engine emits one per-REP score from cycle aggregates — there is no spec rule for deriving a Python per-rep score from the per-frame series, and the two methodologies diverge (Python neutral-80 at the counting frame near lockout vs engine's bottom-aggregate score). §7.4 declares only `scoreRange`; §7.5 doesn't specify the extraction. **NOT added in P1.8b** — the scoreRange gate remains the score assertion. RECOMMEND ratifying: "Python rep score = min `form_score` within that rep's descent→completion window," then assert `|engine − python| ≤ 3` for squat only (jump/chair scoring is interim, above). Awaiting Kd.

- **§7.5 trace-count shortfall (P1.8b Option-B debt, T3 finding G1) — hard gate NOT met:** §7.5 / Part 0 #4 / the P1.8b card require ≥**6 squat + 4 jump + 4 chair** recorded parity sessions; the repo has **3 + 3 + 3**. "9/9 green" = all *present* clips pass, NOT certification. Per the Option-B scope Kd set, this is tracked debt, not a blocker — traces.replay now warns the per-exercise shortfall loudly (no longer the tautology `files.length ≥ 0`, T3 finding G2). Certification unblocks when Kd records the remaining ~3 squat + 1 jump + 1 chair clips (front views included).
- **G3 sign-off needed (T3 finding):** P1's "all invariants CI-enforced" is only PARTIALLY true for these three exercises — reps-exact + view + scoreRange are enforced; fault multisets (I2 exact), ±3 score, and phase-timing tolerances are deferred (below). Needs Kd's explicit acceptance that P1.8b lands with this reduced assertion surface rather than an implicit pass.
- **P1.8b gate debt, still open (T3 P1.6a):** (b) Fault multisets have zero trace coverage — blocked on the same jump-airborne / chair-target template work as the fault mappings above (faultsPending stays). (c) Phase timings are asserted only structurally; a tolerance must be declared before any trace asserts them (§7.4 names none). (d) Kd should spot-check 2–3 re-recorded goldens' expected.reps against the raw videos (gate and fixtures changed in the same PR).

- **SPEC GAP (P1.5, needs ratification at PR #9 merge):** §3.5 says `torso_height = |shoulder_y − hip_y|` but §3.4 row 16 says elevation is normalized "exactly as captured by _StandingCalibration", and the Python capture is `|avg_ankle_y − avg_shoulder_y|` (pose_ws.py:204-207) — the two spec sentences conflict. IMPLEMENTED: the Python capture (shoulder→ankle), because §7.5 parity compares against Python-derived elevations and would otherwise fail by a ~2–2.5× ratio. Merging PR #9 ratifies this; reopen if you read it differently.

## P2.6a — Nutrition and body rulings (2026-07-12)

- Part 2B §3.1/§3.4 vs v1 §6.1 · Meal photos are never persisted anywhere: no R2 object, DB value, cache value, log field, error body, or Sentry payload. The later and more-specific Trust Layer rule wins; photos travel as strict base64 request data, are decoded/analyzed in memory, then discarded.
- Part 2B §3.2 Stage 2 · Portion resolver ships reliable counts plus rung 1 user dishware, rung 3 Appendix B regional priors, and rung 4 global defaults. `portion_source` records the rung. Rung 2 anchor scaling is deferred because Stage 1 returns prose anchors without pixel geometry; follow-up requires a richer vision contract.
- Part 2B §3.2 Stage 3 · Nutrition arithmetic uses the exactly inventoried 130-row curated table first and cache-fronted OpenFoodFacts second. The misnamed salvage `usda.py` is OpenFoodFacts, not USDA. IFCT 2017 is a data-sourcing follow-up.
- v1 §9.3 · OpenFoodFacts calls are exempt from `api_cost_events`: the public API is zero-cost and cache-fronted. This is the explicit exception to the general external-call ledger rule; malformed/unavailable replies degrade to curated-only/empty results.
- Part 2B §3.2 Stage 5 · Per-user dishware memory and correction storage ship now. Confirmation-time changes and later PATCH changes preserve originals in `meal_log_corrections`; per-user bias adaptation and the global regression evaluation set are deferred until telemetry volume exists.
- Part 2B §3.5 · Failed parse or `photo_quality='poor'` issues a cryptographically random retake token stored only as a SHA-256-derived, user-bound Redis key. It is atomically single-use, expires after 10 minutes, bypasses exactly one `meal_scan` quota increment, cannot mint a second token, and fails closed when Redis cannot issue/consume it.
- Part 4 §3.6 / R4.2 · Migration 0005 adds `meal_logs.origin text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'manual' CHECK (origin IN ('photo','manual'))`. Photo-vs-manual is SQL-filtered by a real column, never a JSONB marker. Gamification derives `total_meals=count(*)` and `photo_meals_logged=count(*) FILTER (WHERE origin='photo')`.
- Part 4 §3.6 · The nutrition module owns `body_measurements` CRUD and keeps `users.weight_kg` synchronized to the latest non-null measurement. The users module remains profile-only; direct profile weight edits do not append measurement history.
- v1 §9.3 / P2.5b T3 precedent · A vision scan has no companion application row at spend time, so its `api_cost_events` record is inserted standalone immediately after the provider response and before any result is returned. This keeps the no-spend-escapes-the-ledger invariant; meal confirmation is a later, no-spend transaction.
- Part 2B §3.2 / Groq public pricing · Vision default remains `meta-llama/llama-4-scout-17b-16e-instruct`, with `MEAL_VISION_MODEL` as the swap lever. Groq lists Scout at $0.11/1M input and $0.34/1M output, encoded as integer 110,000/340,000 micro-USD-per-1M constants with BigInt round-half-up. Groq also announces deprecation on 2026-07-17; this is an operational swap risk, not permission to silently change the ruled default.
- 2026-07-12 · P2.2 GAP-2 SUPERSEDED (P2.6a) · Weight history now has ONE write path: body_measurements CRUD (nutrition module) keeps users.weight_kg synced to the latest non-null measurement; profile PATCH weightKg no longer appends a measurement row (it remains for measurement-less users, and is overwritten by the next measurement sync — measurements are the source of truth when present). Replaces the P2.2 ruling "PATCH with changed weightKg appends body_measurements".

A count=3 request therefore decrements quota once and writes three cost rows. A network/parse failure returns no completion → no row for that call (the P2.6a vision-ledger ruling, applied to ORS).
- v1 §12 (P2.6b G3) · Server-side route SCORING (score_and_rank) and WEATHER (check_weather) are NOT ported here — scoring is engine/mobile (§12 puts scoring in @app/engine), weather is a deferred follow-up. /v1/geo/routes/generate returns normalized ORS candidates only (coords, distanceM, elevationGainM, safe/busy/green fractions, isLoop).
- v1 §6.1 / §7.2 / §12 (P2.6b G1) · The two-layer geocode cache (Redis `geo:{lat3}:{lng3}` over the geo_cache Postgres floor, coords rounded to 3 decimals) ships now as MANDATED infra with an INJECTED resolver. It is intentionally RESOLVER-LESS in P2.6b — not dead code: the live reverse-geocode provider and its public endpoint defer to P5 because v1 §12 puts route-name geocoding-on-save on mobile. The seam's caching behavior is locked by the two-layer-cache integration test using a fake resolver.
- routing_provider.py:96-137,270-288 (P2.6b G2) · The salvage's MOCK route generator is a DELIBERATE salvage OMISSION — fabricated geodata violates the trust doctrine, and route_gen is fail-closed. No-key → typed 503; any ORS runtime failure → typed 503 operational (warn-logged, no Sentry — CoachError precedent). There is no offline/mock fallback.
- Part 4 §3.9 (P2.6b G4) · run_schedules is DEFERRED entirely: its `rule jsonb` shape is unspecified in Part 4 and nothing consumes schedules until notifications/mobile. `runs` is READ-ONLY here (list + detail); the run record/sync WRITE path is P5 (mobile, client-generated id + idempotency like workouts).
- v1 §9.3 / Part 0 rule 4 (P2.6b) · ORS cost constant `ORS_ROUTE_COST_MICRO = 0n` (apps/api/src/modules/geo/cost.ts): OpenRouteService's free/OSM tier has no per-call price, so the api_cost_events row is the §9.3 CALL-COUNT requirement (units=1, unit_type='route', provider='ors'), not a dollar charge. One-line updatable the day a paid ORS plan is adopted.
- Part 4 §3.9 (P2.6b minor) · `runs.splits` (jsonb) is OMITTED from the P2.6b read response — its shape is unspecified and P5 owns the writer; adding it now would invent a shape (R0.2). Run detail returns the polyline (owner-only) + core fields; splits join when P5 defines them.

## P2.7 — Mongo→PG migration rulings (2026-07-13; approved at the P2.7 gate)

- Part I §7b / Part 0 (P2.7 split) · P2.7 is split (like P2.6/P1.8) — one migration-worth per chat exceeds the 🔴 ceiling. Order: P2.7a INVENTORY (read-only, apps/api/tools/migrate-mongo/INVENTORY.md) → P2.7b harness + `users` → P2.7c workouts+sets+templates → P2.7d meal_logs+body_measurements → P2.7e coach+running → P2.7f verify gates + prod runbook.
- v1 §7.4 vs Part 4 §7 (P2.7 G3, spec-vs-spec CONFLICT) · v1 §7.4 says "ObjectId→UUID with a lookup table"; Part 4 §7:867-871 says UUIDv5-deterministic "without a lookup table". Part 4 §7 WINS (Part 0 precedence: later + more-specific part; Part 4 §0 amends earlier parts). Migration uses `id = UUIDv5(NAMESPACE_AIHG, mongo _id hex)`, NO lookup table; source id kept in `legacy_mongo_id`. CLAUDE.md:305/360 ("mapping table") echo the superseded v1 framing.
- v1 §7.4 argon2id vs Part 4 §7 bcrypt (P2.7, RESOLVED) · v1 §7.4's "upgrade to argon2id on next login" is moot — P2.1 shipped bcrypt-only (auth/service.ts:17 BCRYPT_COST=10; auth/repo.ts:70,86 write hash_algo='bcrypt'; DECISIONS 2026-07-11 GAP-1). Migration preserves Mongo bcrypt as hash_algo='bcrypt'; users.hash_algo CHECK allows argon2id but nothing writes it. No open conflict.
- Part 4 §7:868 (P2.7 G2) · NAMESPACE_AIHG frozen once = `4fc832e8-4827-4475-bf8a-e72cc4b611c7` (generated via crypto.randomUUID). Must NEVER change or every migrated id drifts. Referenced only at part4:868; no spec value existed, so this is the project-frozen value.
- R1.4 (P2.7 G4) · UUIDv5 = a ~30-line in-house SHA-1 RFC-4122 impl (tested against RFC vectors), NOT the `uuid` npm package — keeps the zero-extra-dep ethos; `node:crypto` provides only v4. Lands in P2.7b.
- P2.7a inventory OUTPUT · ~15 blocking items surfaced for P2.7b: the workout_sets unroll is DATA-ONLY (legacy `exercises` is an untyped list → needs a mongodump, G1); plus rulings owed on kcal recompute, unmatched-exercise fallback, embedded-subdoc id derivation, onboarding-field data loss, OAuth/role/profilePicture dispositions, meal_type/fiber drop, workouts-legacy-id column, running polyline encoding, and run_schedules.rule shape. See INVENTORY.md "BLOCKING items".

## P2.7 — clean-start + full-migration decisions (2026-07-13; Kd ruled)

- v1 §7.4 / Part 4 §7 / R0.1 (P2.7 migration approach = B) · The full P2.7 Mongo→PG migration IS built per §7 (spec is law; a DEVIATION PROPOSAL to skip it — on the grounds the old data is 18 dev/test users with no real user base — was RAISED and REJECTED by Kd; Part I.5 "rejected → spec stands"). The script is built AND verified end-to-end against the live dev Mongo (docker `aihg-mongo`) as the fixture: §7 gates (counts ±0, sampled user/workout/meal counts, 20 bcrypt logins, UUIDv5 cross-ref spot-checks).
- (P2.7 clean production start) · PRODUCTION launches with an EMPTY database — the dev/test data (18 users, 230 plan-level workouts, 16 meals, 11 coach threads, 8 runs, 17 routes, 1 schedule, 1 measurement) is NOT imported into production. Rationale: production-grade hygiene — importing test accounts/skeleton workouts would permanently contaminate real users, metrics, and Form Score™/leaderboards. The verified migration (above) is a correctness artifact + future insurance, not the production seed.
- (P2.7a inventory now DATA-VERIFIED, live Mongo scan 2026-07-13) · Corrections to the code-derived inventory: (1) auth+ml+onboarding are ONE merged `users` collection (18 docs; 17 password, 1 googleId, 18 email) — §7's "merge duplicate auth/ml email pairs" does NOT apply. (2) `workout_sessions.exercises[]` items are PRESCRIPTIONS `{id,name,category?,sets,reps,rest}` (or the full denormalized exercise doc) — 0 of 230 carry any per-set performance; the new `workout_sets` rich fields (rep_scores, fault_counts, form-per-set, view, mode, hold_ms, tempo, rom, calibration) have NO legacy source → all NULL; unroll = expand each item's `sets` count into set_index rows with prescribed `reps`. (3) `active_seconds_by_exercise` is NOT persisted → the §7 per-exercise MET kcal recompute is impossible; keep stored `calories_burned` (calc_version=0) [G-kcal, pending final ruling]. (4) `workout_templates` = 0 rows. (5) exercises = 58 (matches Part 0 canonical count).

## P2.7c — workouts + sets + gamification recompute (2026-07-13; Kd ruled at plan gate)
- (P2.7c GAP1 = a) exercise_id resolution uses an explicit **14-name→slug map** (tools/migrate-mongo/exerciseNames.ts, `NAME_TO_SLUG`) — the 230 legacy workouts reference EXACTLY 14 distinct exercise names (live-scanned). A name whose slug has no seeded catalog row TODAY (only squat/jump_squat/chair_squat are seeded; the other 55 land at P4) is SKIPPED + quality-flagged `unknown_exercise` (mirrors the sync path, workouts/repo.ts:70). The map is a REVIEWED CONSTANTS TABLE (P1.8a precedent): a purely mechanical derivation is WRONG — seeded slugs are singular ("squat", seed.ts:198) vs legacy plurals ("Squats") — so each row is hand-set with catalog evidence. 3 of 14 resolve today; 8 target canonical Part 2 §6 catalog slugs (reconcile at P4); 3 (Arnold Shoulder Press §6:731, 1-Arm Lat Pulldown, 1 Leg Box Squat) are NOT in the canonical 58 → permanently skipped.
- (P2.7c GAP1 re-run correction, T3-B finding 2026-07-13, Kd ruled) An INCREMENTAL re-run after P4 seeds a previously-skipped name does NOT self-heal (the earlier "resolves automatically on re-run" claim was WRONG): set_index is GLOBAL and assigned over currently-resolvable items only, so newly-resolved items shift indices and collide with already-persisted (workout_id, set_index) rows (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING keeps the stale row); and the parent `workouts` row is ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING, so `sets_count`/`total_reps`/`quality_flags` never heal. To pick up exercises seeded after the initial migration, do a **CLEAN re-migrate** — clear the workout tables and re-run (from empty the indexing is consistent) — NOT an incremental re-run. Fine because production starts empty (this is a dev/test correctness artifact). Same-seed re-runs ARE a true no-op (deterministic UUIDv5 PK + ON CONFLICT), which is the idempotency property that matters during the migration window, and it is tested.
- (P2.7c GAP2) `workout_sets.duration_ms` is NOT NULL with no legacy source (0/230 carry per-set performance) → migrated as **0**.
- (P2.7c G-kcal, DEVIATION from §7 — T3-A finding, Kd ruled 2026-07-13) Spec §7 (04-part4-database.md:887-892) says legacy `kcal_*` is RECOMPUTED at migration with `calc_version=1` + the new MET table (2B). This is IMPOSSIBLE for the legacy data: `active_seconds_by_exercise` (per-exercise time, the MET input) was never persisted, and per GAP2 each migrated `workout_sets.duration_ms=0` — so a faithful recompute would zero out every workout's calories, destroying the real stored numbers. RULING: **keep the stored `calories_burned` at `kcal_calc_version=0`** (legacy provenance), NOT a §7 recompute. This is an explicit DEVIATION from §7's "one sanctioned history recomputation" clause, ratifying the P2.7a "[G-kcal, pending final ruling]" note (DECISIONS.md:205); the spec's recompute presumes an input the legacy schema never captured.
- (P2.7c GAP3) `workouts` keeps **UUIDv5-only traceability** (id = UUIDv5(sessionHex)); NO `legacy_mongo_id` column added, NO schema change / no migration. Set ids = UUIDv5(sessionHex:globalSetIndex) (G-subid).
- (P2.7c verify gate, Kd correction) The workouts count gate is honest w.r.t. fail-soft skipping: PG matched (by UUIDv5 id) must equal the number of MIGRATABLE sessions (transform-accepted = Mongo − skipped), and insert errors surface as PG < expected. Sets gate = PG rows on migrated workouts == Σ prescribed sets over RESOLVABLE names. Streaks gate = every migrated user with ≥1 workout has a streaks row. Gates re-derive expected via the tested pure transform (verifies the DB write path, not just the transform).
- (P2.7c recompute reuse) Gamification is recomputed by calling gamification/service.ts `onWorkoutSynced({sql}, userId, null)` per migrated user (NOT reimplemented) — it replays streaks from workout-day history and awards achievements idempotently (§7:882-884); `safeTimeZone(null)='UTC'` matches legacy utcnow day-math. Precondition: target DB seeded (exercises + achievements FK targets) — `tsx src/db/seed.ts` (idempotent).
- (P2.7c reader infra) mongo.ts reader generalized to normalize ALL top-level ObjectId fields → hex (was `_id` only), so `workout_sessions.user_id` arrives as a hex string and transforms stay string-typed/Zod-parseable (the reader's documented intent). Users stage unaffected (its only ObjectId is `_id`).

## P2.7d — meals + body_measurements (2026-07-13; Kd ruled at plan gate)
- (P2.7d live scan) meal_logs=16 (ONE user 6a0d468a…, a P2.7c workout user; keys meal_type/food_name/quantity/kcal/protein_g/carbs_g/fat_g/fiber_g/notes/consumed_at). body_measurements=1 (same user; weight_kg + 7 *_cm + body_fat_pct). Both target tables HAVE a `legacy_mongo_id` column (trust.ts) — traceability + verify gate use it (unlike workouts).
- (P2.7d GAP-A, the meal item — Kd ruled) `meal_logs.items` is NOT NULL jsonb re-validated by `@app/shared` mealItemSchema on EVERY read (nutrition/repo.ts:60 → a nonconforming item 500s the read). The schema REQUIRES per item: `gramsPoint>0`, `gramsRange:[>0,>0]`, `nutritionSource ∈ {curated,openfoodfacts}` (nutrition.ts:4-15) — legacy meals have NONE (no grams; `quantity` is a serving count, not grams; no source). RULING: build ONE synthetic item per meal — `gramsPoint=100`, `gramsRange=[70,130]` (placeholder), `portionSource='legacy'` (the honest "not a real measurement" flag; 'legacy' IS in the enum), `nutritionSource='curated'` (least-wrong; the enum has no legacy value). The ROW's `nutrition_sources=['legacy_model']` (text[], no enum) carries honest provenance. `quantity` is NOT used as grams (misleading). This fabricates a portion size, flagged via portionSource='legacy'; acceptable because production starts empty (dev/test correctness artifact).
- (P2.7d GAP-B, drop) `meal_type`, `fiber_g`, `notes`, `quantity` have no target column → dropped.
- (P2.7d GAP-C, origin) Some `notes` read "Estimated from photo…" but there is NO structured photo field → `origin='manual'` for all (conservative; the `photo_meal` badge simply won't award — never a fabricated 'photo').
- (P2.7d meal row fixed values) `confirmed=true` (user saved them), `kcal_low=round(kcal*0.7)`/`kcal_high=round(kcal*1.3)` (§7 ±30% band), `portion_source='legacy'`, `calc_version=0`, `legacy_mongo_id=_id`, ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING. Row totals = the single item (kcal/macros).
- (P2.7d GAP-D, weight refresh) After body inserts, `users.weight_kg` is refreshed to each user's LATEST measurement (mirrors nutrition/repo.ts refreshWeight; body history is the authoritative weight per §3.6/DECISIONS 2026-07-12) — overwrites the P2.7b-migrated weight for that user. weight_kg clamped >999.99→null (numeric(5,2)); `*_cm`+body_fat_pct → `metrics` jsonb (nonneg finite only, per the read-side z.record guard).
- (P2.7d GAP-E, gamification) Re-run gamification/service.ts `onMealLogged({sql}, userId, null)` per meal-affected user (REUSE, not reimpl) — awards meal badges (first_meal) idempotently; also lazily reconciles that user's streak to today (identical to their next live read, DECISIONS GAP-5; harmless for old data).

Now samples only transform-accepted workouts (transformWorkout(doc)!==null), using row.id/row.userId — absence-from-PG can no longer masquerade as a mapping failure. Consequence: a migrated user who ALSO has a natively-synced workout would inflate the PG per-user count → a false mismatch on a MIXED db. Harmless on greenfield prod (empty) and on the verified dev cutover (per_user_mismatches=0); best available given the schema. Recorded so a future re-run against a mixed db isn't surprised. No fix.

## argon2id rehash-on-login (2026-07-14; the P2.1 GAP-1 deferral, owed before P2.8)
- (v1 §6.1 / R1.4) Password hashing upgraded to argon2id via `@node-rs/argon2` (prebuilt native binaries, no node-gyp; ships its own .d.ts). `bcryptjs` KEPT — it verifies legacy bcrypt hashes. Params = OWASP minimum: memoryCost 19456 KiB, timeCost 2, parallelism 1 (`ARGON2ID_OPTS`, service.ts). `algorithm` passed as the numeric literal `2` (Algorithm.Argon2id) with `as const`: the library exports Algorithm as a `const enum`, which cannot be imported as a value under isolatedModules (R2.1/TS2748); the `$argon2id$` + `m=19456,t=2,p=1` output format is asserted in the unit tests as the guard.
- (v1 §6.1) `PasswordHasher` interface changed from `{ hash, compare }` to `{ algo, hash, verify(pw,hash,algo), needsRehash(algo) }`. `verify` dispatches on the STORED algo (bcrypt→bcrypt.compare, argon2id→argon2.verify) with an exhaustive `never` default (R2.4). NB argon2.verify(hashed, password) takes the hash FIRST (opposite to bcrypt.compare) — pinned by the round-trip unit test. Only auth service.ts (defines) + routes.ts (wires) consume it; no other module.
- (v1 §6.1) Rehash-on-login: after a successful verify, `if (needsRehash(user.hashAlgo)) setPasswordHash(argon2id hash)`. BEST-EFFORT — a rehash write failure is swallowed + logged (event `auth.password_rehash_failed`) and NEVER fails an already-valid login (deliberate R2.5 exception, same swallow pattern as the existing email sends). Awaited (not fire-and-forget) so the upgrade is durable before the session returns AND observable by the routes test. Migrated bcrypt users upgrade transparently on their next login; a re-login is a byte-identical no-op (needsRehash false).
- (v1 §6.1 accepted limitation) The timing-equalizer DUMMY_HASH is now a single module-level argon2id hash. One dummy cannot equalize login timing across a MIXED bcrypt+argon2id population: a not-yet-upgraded bcrypt user's login (bcrypt.compare) times differently from an unknown-email attempt (argon2.verify on the dummy) until that user rehashes. Self-healing as the population migrates; accepted rather than maintaining two dummies.
- (defense-in-depth) A non-null password_hash always carries a valid hash_algo (migration invariant, tools/migrate-mongo/collections/users.ts:65: password null ⇒ algo null, else 'bcrypt'), and login short-circuits on password_hash null before any verify — so hash_algo-null-with-a-hash is unreachable. Still handled: login/changePassword treat a null hashAlgo as fail-closed (invalid_credentials / no_password) rather than crashing. `repo.toHashAlgo` validates the nullable text column into `HashAlgo | null`.
- (no schema migration) users.hash_algo CHECK already allows 'argon2id' (identity.ts:37, migration 0001) — this card adds NO migration. `DUMMY_HASH` exported from service.ts solely so a unit test can assert it is argon2id.

## web repoint — Card 1: auth → httpOnly-cookie on the new /v1 API (2026-07-15)
- (SCOPE, Kd-ruled) The "apps/web repointed to the new API" P2.8 prerequisite is NOT a config flip: the web ran the OLD auth model (localStorage access/refresh tokens + `Authorization: Bearer` on every client) while the new API is httpOnly-cookie-only with no tokens in any response body (shared/src/auth.ts:52 authUserSchema; DECISIONS 2026-07-11). v1 §13 lists the SPA's changes but does not itemize this repoint; v1 §6.1:439 fixes the target model ("rotating refresh tokens (httpOnly cookie on web)"). Decomposed into cards: ①auth ②users/profile ③progress/gamification/exercises ④coach ⑤nutrition ⑥running/geo ⑦recommendation-or-drop. Card ① is this one.
- (BRANCH STRATEGY, Kd-ruled) The repoint cannot be staged client-by-client on a working app — auth is all-or-nothing (cookie vs localStorage), so the moment auth flips, every not-yet-repointed client loses the localStorage token it depends on. Therefore ALL web-repoint cards land as commits on ONE branch `web-repoint` (each with its own T3), and it merges to master only when the web fully runs on the new API — which IS the P2.8 cutover moment. `master` stays deployable (old-backend web) until then (Part I §6).
- (Google OAuth DEFERRED, Kd-ruled) v1 §6.1:438 lists Google OAuth in the auth module, but P2.1 shipped email/password only and the new API has NO /v1/auth/google route (verified). So the web's Google buttons are hidden behind `GOOGLE_LOGIN_ENABLED=false` (Login.jsx, Register.jsx) and the /auth/google/success route + import are removed from App.jsx. Google OAuth on the new API is its own later card; `pages/GoogleAuthSuccess.jsx` is left in-tree but is now ORPHANED dead code (no route, no import) that still does `localStorage.setItem('accessToken')` (:31) and calls the now-wrong `/auth/me` path (:35) — unreachable, so inert; the Google card must rewrite or delete it (T3 finding).
- (INTERIM behavior regression — onboarding gating goes inert) `authUserSchema` (shared/src/auth.ts:52) has NO `onboardingCompleted` field — onboarding is a `users`-module concern per v1 §6.1:442, not auth — so /v1/auth/me and /v1/auth/login never return it. The three sites that gate on it — ProtectedRoute.jsx:44, :54 and Login.jsx:33 — compare `=== false`, so `undefined` makes them all false: **onboarding is never enforced for anyone** on this branch. Fails OPEN (no redirect loop, no user trap), and the branch can't reach master before P2.8, so it is accepted as an interim — but it IS a real regression, and restoring it is OWED BY the users/profile card (②) when /v1/users/me supplies the field. (T3 finding: was undocumented; recorded here.)
- (INTERIM known-broken — the still-old clients) Login no longer writes `localStorage.accessToken`, so every not-yet-repointed client that injects `Bearer <localStorage token>` now sends `Bearer null` and breaks ON THE BRANCH: mlApi.js:10, coachApi.js:17, nutritionApi.js:31, utils/storage.js:28, and Settings.jsx:401 (handleDeleteAccount, untouched by Card 1). This is the planned multi-card consequence, not a defect — PROVE for Card 1 must NOT be expected to exercise coach / ML-profile / nutrition / delete-account. Each is repointed by its own card before the branch merges. (T3 finding: recorded explicitly.)
- (compat shim, interim) The new user shape exposes `displayName`; 6 display sites still read `user?.fullName` (+1 `user?.profilePicture`, which the new shape lacks and which stays undefined behind optional chaining). `normalizeUser` in AuthContext.jsx aliases `fullName: displayName` on both getMe and login so Card 1 stays contained to the auth layer. The users/profile card (②) migrates those sites and REMOVES the shim.
- (R10.2 reconciled) The authApi 401→refresh→retry-once interceptor retries a POST, which R10.2 forbids for network-failure retries. Reconciled: the retry fires ONLY on `error.response.status === 401` (network errors have no `.response` → never retried), and in this API auth is a preHandler — a 401 is rejected BEFORE the handler runs, so the write never executed and re-sending after cookie rotation is safe. Capped at one retry via `config._retried`; /v1/auth/login and /v1/auth/refresh are excluded from the interceptor so it cannot recurse. (T3 confirmed the reasoning holds.)

## web repoint — Card 2: per-user storage keying + displayName migration (2026-07-15)
- (CARD-1 REGRESSION — found in Card 2 grounding, FIXED here) `utils/storage.js getUserId()` decoded the JWT out of `localStorage.accessToken` to key every per-user bucket (`userKey(k) = user_${id}_${k}`). Card 1 moved sessions to httpOnly cookies (v1 §6.1), which JS cannot read — so getUserId() returned **'guest' for every account, permanently**. Consumers: ActiveWorkout, ExerciseLibrary, PreWorkout, WorkoutBuilder, and syncQueue.js:13 (the OFFLINE SYNC QUEUE). Impact: all accounts on a device shared one bucket, so on a shared browser user A's unflushed workouts sat in the same queue B would flush under B's cookie → workouts mis-attributed to the wrong user, against R10.3's intent. FIX: `storage.setCurrentUserId(id)` is pushed in by AuthContext on session-restore/login/logout; getUserId() returns it ('guest' when logged out). Regression tests: utils/storage.test.js (isolation, logout→guest, per-user queue buckets, and an explicit guard that keying no longer derives from a token). NB Card 1's T3 saw storage.js:28 but classified it as ordinary Bearer-null breakage — it was a keying break, not an API-call break.
- (PLAN AMENDMENT, declared at implementation — R1.2) `syncClient.js`'s module-scope app-load flush (`flushSyncQueue()` at import) was REMOVED. It only ever worked because the user id was synchronously decodable from a localStorage JWT; with the id now arriving asynchronously from /v1/auth/me, an import-time flush reads the 'guest' bucket and would silently never flush the signed-in user's queued workouts. AuthContext kicks that flush immediately after adopting the session id (`adoptSession`). The `online` listener STAYS at module scope.
- (NOT EQUIVALENT — accepted delta, T3 Card 2) The AuthContext-kicked flush is **not** a like-for-like replacement for the removed import-time flush, and the code comment previously implied it was. Old: fired on EVERY app load (the id was synchronously in localStorage). New: fires only when `/v1/auth/me` SUCCEEDS. So if getMe fails at app load (network blip / API 5xx) while the session cookie is still valid, the id stays 'guest', no flush runs for that page-session, and the `online` listener can then only address the empty guest bucket. ACCEPTED: it is a **liveness delay bounded by one page-session, never data loss** — the queue is untouched and any later reload or login flushes it — and it is intrinsic to the cookie migration (there is no token to read offline). Recorded rather than fixed.
- (Kd-ruled — LEGACY BUCKET ORPHANING; scope corrected by T3) Per-user localStorage buckets — including the offline workout queue — are keyed `user_<id>_*`. Pre-repoint that id is the OLD Mongo ObjectId (from the old JWT); post-repoint it is the new UUID (§7 uuidv5 mapping), so unflushed workouts + WorkoutBuilder drafts orphan under an address the app no longer reads. NOT fixed in code: the client cannot derive mongoId from uuid, so a shim would have to "adopt any orphaned non-guest bucket" — reintroducing the shared-browser hazard this card just closed. **SCOPE (T3 correction): this is a dev/test-cutover issue, NOT a production hazard** — production launches with an EMPTY database (DECISIONS 2026-07-13, recorded at RUNBOOK/cutover.md:11-13), so there are no users and no buckets to orphan. NOW A CHECKBOX in RUNBOOK/cutover.md's prerequisites (that file already existed — T3 rightly flagged that "owed by a future card" is how such an item gets lost).
- (T3 Card 2 finding 1 — FIXED, R10.3) `flushRun` bound the queue KEY once at run start, but identity is bound at SEND time: `postSync` carries whatever httpOnly cookie is ambient and has no user binding. A session change mid-run (logout + a different login while the loop awaits) would keep draining user A's bucket while the server attributed those workouts to user B — the residual half of the same shared-browser hazard this card set out to close. FIX: `flushRun` captures `const owner = getUserId()` and returns immediately before any `post(entry)` if identity has moved; the abandoned entries stay queued for their real owner (neither dropped nor sent). Regression test: syncQueue.test.js "abandons the run when the session changes mid-flush". NB `syncApi` (syncClient.js:21-25) has NO timeout, so a hung POST holds a run open indefinitely and widens the window — the owner check makes that harmless (correctness no longer depends on run length), so the timeout is REPORTED not fixed (R1.1), for the sync card.
- (LANDMINE recorded for the Google OAuth card — T3, report-only) AuthContext exposes `setUser` raw in the context value (:123) and `pages/GoogleAuthSuccess.jsx:37` calls it directly — that path would set a session WITHOUT `adoptSession`, keying the user to 'guest' and re-opening the bucket/queue hazard. Currently UNREACHABLE (Card 1 deleted the route + import; the file is orphaned), so not a live defect and not fixed here (R1.1). The Google OAuth card MUST route session adoption through `adoptSession` (or stop exporting `setUser`).
- (interim shim REMOVED as promised) The 6 `user?.fullName` sites (Sidebar.jsx:149,153,188; Coach.jsx:519; Dashboard.jsx:262; Running.jsx:136) now read `user?.displayName`, and Card 1's `normalizeUser` alias is deleted from AuthContext.
- (scope, verified) `userService.getProfile/updateProfile` are DEAD CODE — the only live userService call is Onboarding.jsx:244 `completeOnboarding`, which is blocked by the onboarding-storage gap. Settings' two profile forms are ~80% onboarding fields (age/gender/height/targetWeight; fitnessLevel/fitnessGoals/availableEquipment/sessionDuration/preferredWorkoutTime/exerciseFrequency/medicalConditions) and its avatar upload has no target — so Settings' profile surface, the Onboarding wizard and the 3 onboarding gate sites are all LEFT UNTOUCHED on the old backend. Nothing deleted; all owed to the onboarding-storage card.
- (out of scope, REPORTED not fixed — R1.1) `syncClient.test.js` "is a no-op when VITE_API_URL is not configured" FAILS ON MASTER TOO (verified by stashing: identical failure, 1 failed/6 passed). Vitest loads `apps/web/.env`, which sets VITE_API_URL, so flushSyncQueue()'s guard doesn't fire and flush() reaches `window.localStorage` in the node env. The test's comment assumes VITE_API_URL is unset — true in CI (no .env committed), false on a dev machine. Pre-existing env-dependent test bug; not touched by this card.
- (testing gap, honest) The `adoptSession → flushSyncQueue` coupling is NOT unit-tested — that needs jsdom/RTL, which the web package doesn't have (vitest.config.js is node-only; adding it = new deps, R1.4). Covered only by the manual browser smoke. The storage keying itself IS unit-tested.

## onboarding-storage: fitness-profile storage on the new API (2026-07-15)
- (THE GAP, verified) v1 §6.1:442 assigns "onboarding data" to the `users` module but Part 4 defines NO storage for it — the §3.1 users DDL (04-part4-database.md:116-134) has no age/gender/height/fitness_level/goals/equipment columns. P2.7's migration therefore DROPped those Mongo fields (tools/migrate-mongo/INVENTORY.md:45, "(no columns) DROP — no target; the queued onboarding-storage gap"), which also starves Part 2B §4.1:358's content-based scorer (goal 40 · difficulty 20 · equipment 20 · duration 10 — precisely the dropped fields) that the spec calls the correct architecture. This card builds that storage. API-only and additive (the old web still POSTs /users/onboarding to backend-ml), so it merges to master normally — unlike the web-repoint cards.
- (PLACEMENT, Kd-ruled — Option B of two presented) A separate 1:1 table `user_fitness_profiles` (user_id IS the PK), NOT new columns on `users`. Rationale: purely additive migration with zero lock/rewrite risk on the auth-hot `users` table; leaves the spec's published §3.1 DDL intact rather than amending it with 11 nullable columns; onboarding data is a cohesive unit the future scorer reads together. Cost: one PK join on profile reads (`selectProfile` LEFT JOINs it for `onboarding_completed`). Weight is NOT duplicated — it stays on `users.weight_kg` (Part 4 §3.1) and the wizard's weight step uses PATCH /v1/users/me.
- (VALUE SETS — ported, never derived; R0.2) Every enum is copied verbatim from the salvage source backend-auth/src/models/User.js:44-98: gender male|female|other|prefer_not_to_say · fitness_level beginner|intermediate|advanced · fitness_goals weight_loss|muscle_gain|general_fitness|flexibility|endurance|posture|stress_relief (7) · available_equipment none|dumbbells|resistance_bands|kettlebells|pull_up_bar (5) · preferred_workout_time morning|afternoon|evening. Enforced as `text` + CHECK per Part 4 §1 (never PG enums); the two array columns are `text[]` with the value set enforced in Zod, following the existing `exercises.equipment`/`muscles` precedent (db/schema/catalog.ts:31-32) — Part 4 §1's JSONB policy forbids JSONB here since the scorer will filter on these.
- (BOUNDS — Kd-approved, NOT spec values) Neither the spec nor the Mongo model bounds these numerics; the following are sanity rails invented for this card and approved at the plan gate: age 13–120 · heightCm 50–300 · targetWeightKg positive/<1000/2dp (mirrors weightKg + numeric(5,2)) · exerciseFrequency 1–7 · sessionDurationMin 5–240 · medicalConditions trimmed, ≤2000 chars. They live in Zod only — the DDL does not encode them.
- (fitness_level DEFAULT, Kd-approved) Stored NULL until the user answers. The old Mongo model defaulted it to 'beginner'; we deliberately do not — unanswered is not beginner, and a future scorer can treat NULL as beginner if it chooses. Storing the guess would launder it into data.
- (PUT semantics) `PUT /v1/users/me/fitness-profile` is a FULL-DOCUMENT replace: an omitted field is written as NULL. That makes it idempotent by construction (R3.5) — the same body twice yields the same row — so it needs no Idempotency-Key. CONSEQUENCE, accepted: a client that sends `{}` clears the profile (and `onboarding_completed` → false, re-triggering the wizard). True PUT semantics; the wizard always submits the whole document. No data beyond the profile is affected.
- (GET returns the EMPTY profile, not a 404) No row is the common case (a user who has not onboarded), so the GET returns all-nulls with `updatedAt: null` — the wizard renders blank instead of branching on an error, and no timestamp is synthesized for a row that was never written. `userProfileSchema.onboardingCompleted` COALESCEs to false for the same reason.
- (onboardingCompleted on /v1/users/me — scope addition, Kd-approved) The field is added to the users profile view. This is the interim regression DECISIONS 2026-07-15 (web Card 1) recorded as OWED: the web's three gate sites (ProtectedRoute.jsx:44,:54; Login.jsx:33) compare `=== false`, so with the field absent from the auth view onboarding is enforced for nobody on the web-repoint branch. This card supplies the field; the web card that consumes it still owes the wiring.
- (DPDP — CORRECTION to the plan's premise; a real obligation, not covered by the FK) The plan asserted "the DPDP hard-delete cascade covers it for free". That is FALSE: Part 4 §5.2:829 ANONYMIZES the users row to a tombstone ("row kept so FKs from audit/invoices resolve") and never deletes it, so `ON DELETE CASCADE` NEVER FIRES on account deletion. §5.2's real mechanism is its explicit Day-14 DELETE list — which enumerates `auth_identities` even though that table already has CASCADE, proving the cascade is not what does the work. `user_fitness_profiles` holds age/gender/height and `medical_conditions` (health data, sensitive under DPDP), so it MUST be added to (a) the §5.2 Day-14 explicit DELETE list and (b) the §5.2 JSON-export list. Both belong to the Day-14/export worker card, which DECISIONS 2026-07-11 records as QUEUED and unbuilt. Recorded here and in a schema comment (db/schema/identity.ts) so that card inherits it. The FK CASCADE is KEPT as defense-in-depth (correct per Part 4 §1: a fitness profile is meaningless without its user; flagged inline as §1 requires) and is proven by a db.migration test — but it is not the DPDP path.
- (active-only upsert) The upsert is `INSERT … SELECT FROM users WHERE id=$1 AND status='active' … ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE`. The FK proves the user EXISTS but says nothing about status (§5.2 soft-deletes), and a check-then-insert would TOCTOU against a concurrent deletion; the SELECT makes "active user only" atomic — a deleted user's SELECT yields no row, nothing inserts, RETURNING is empty → 401.
- (no duplicates in the array fields) `fitnessGoals`/`availableEquipment` reject duplicate values rather than silently deduping (R2.3 parse-don't-validate): a repeated goal would double-weight Part 2B §4's scorer. The old Mongo model permitted duplicates; this is stricter by choice.
- (MIGRATION NUMBERING TRAP — repo-wide, found by this card) drizzle-kit numbers migrations from the journal's 0-based `idx`, but this repo's files are `idx + 1` (`0001_init` is idx 0), so EVERY generated migration lands one behind and must be renamed — drizzle generated `0005_user_fitness_profiles.sql`, colliding with the existing `0005_meal_logs_origin.sql`. The established fix (verified in commit 34438bf: `0005_meal_logs_origin.sql` shipped with `meta/0004_snapshot.json`) is to rename the SQL file AND its `_journal.json` tag to idx+1, leaving the snapshot at drizzle's own idx. Done here: file + tag `0006_user_fitness_profiles`, snapshot `meta/0005_snapshot.json`. Every future migration card hits this — rename before committing.
- (T3 RESOLUTION, 2026-07-15 — reviewed in a fresh chat per Part I §7c) T3 found NO blocking violations. Two advisories: (1) R9.2 — the accepted `PUT {}` full-clear semantics were exercised only via a partial body; FIXED by adding an explicit empty-body test (users.fitness.routes.test.ts, "PUT {} is the extreme replace") pinning that {} NULLs every field, flips onboarding_completed→false, and REPLACES rather than deletes the row (updatedAt stays a string). Full suite now 252 passed. (2) R11.4 — self-audit "PROVE green" is container-lifetime-bound; the closing gate is CI-on-Neon (below), not local PG16. Security pass clean (authn/tenancy/IDOR-none, parse, idempotency, SQL, no medical_conditions log leak). DPDP correction judged sound.
- (DPDP ESCALATION, T3 recommendation — Kd decision owed) Merging this card makes the queued Day-14/export worker card a DPDP EXPOSURE, not just a spec checkbox: a deleted user's medical_conditions (health data) now persists indefinitely on user_fitness_profiles until that worker ships (§5.2 tombstones users, so the FK CASCADE never collects it). RECOMMENDATION: promote the Day-14/export worker card in the queue ahead of non-compliance work. Recorded for Kd; not actioned here (out of card scope).
- (DPDP ESCALATION — RULED 2026-07-16: ACCEPT + PROMOTE) Kd delegated the call to the implementing chat's recommendation ("do which one you recommend"), so recording it as such rather than as an independent operator ruling. DECISION: ACCEPT the process-only guard and MERGE; the Day-14 hard-delete + JSON-export worker card is hereby PROMOTED to next-priority ahead of other non-compliance work (T3's recommendation). Rationale: production launches with an EMPTY database (DECISIONS 2026-07-13; RUNBOOK/cutover.md:11-13), so there are zero real users and zero real medical_conditions rows today — the exposure is theoretical at this instant and becomes real the moment the first user registers post-cutover. Blocking instead would stall the P2.8 critical path (the old backend cannot be decommissioned) behind a sizeable BullMQ card. THE PROMOTION IS THE PRICE OF THE ACCEPT: this card must land before real users exist, i.e. before/with P2.8 cutover — it is no longer a "someday" item.
- (NEON PRIMARY BRANCH WAS EMPTY — root cause of PR #30's red CI; repaired 2026-07-16) CI's `drizzle migrations on Neon branch` job died in <1s. NOT a fault in 0006 and NOT a bad GitHub NEON_API_KEY (the branch `ci-29440982870` was created fine, log line 18:33:37). Cause: the free-tier Neon branch had reset AGAIN (3rd occurrence — see HANDOFF:123 for 2026-07-13), leaving the PRIMARY branch (`br-twilight-darkness-aotigisp`) with **0 tables and no drizzle bookkeeping**; CI branches FROM primary (`init_source: parent-data`), so every CI run cloned an empty DB. Prior PRs (e.g. #28) stayed green only because they added NO migration — drizzle had nothing to apply and exited 0. 0006 was the first new migration since the reset, so it was the first to actually touch the broken DB. REPAIR: new connection string (host ep-plain-thunder → ep-wispy-rain) into gitignored apps/api/.env; `drizzle-kit migrate` → 6/6 applied, 44 public tables; seed re-run (idempotent); full api suite against REAL Neon = 33 files / 252 passed. CI re-run then went green (migrations job 58s, i.e. actually executing). LESSON for future cards: a green CI on a no-migration PR proves NOTHING about Neon's schema state; if the Neon branch resets again, repair primary FIRST (migrate + seed) or every subsequent migration PR reds.

## Vision model swap + format-tolerant parsing (2026-07-16; Kd-approved option 1 during web Card 5a)
- (TRIGGER — the Card 5a smoke, second CORS-class catch) Kd's browser smoke 422'd ("retake photo") on a clear photo. Root cause, proven by replaying the EXACT adapter request against live Groq: BOTH real vision models return field formats the strict evidence schema rejects — Scout emitted `confidence: 0.9` (schema: enum high/medium/low) and `fill_level: "full"` (schema: number|null); Qwen emitted `photo_quality: "Good"` and `fill_level: "N/A"`. Every real scan died; the 250+ green tests never saw it because they use a fake provider that answers in perfect schema shape. The real completions are preserved VERBATIM as fixtures in nutrition.unit.test.ts (R9.5: failing tests written first).
- (MEAL_VISION_MODEL default → `qwen/qwen3.6-27b`, supersedes DECISIONS 2026-07-12 P2.6a) Groq decommissions Scout 2026-07-17 (email 2026-07-16). qwen3.6-27b is the ONLY vision-capable Groq replacement (console.groq.com/docs/vision, checked 2026-07-16). Qwen defaults to reasoning, which burned max_tokens before the JSON → the adapter passes `reasoning_effort: "none"` for `qwen/`-prefixed models (Groq docs/reasoning; the parameter is Qwen-only, so it is conditional).
- (Price constants re-quoted per Part 0 rule 4) VISION_INPUT/OUTPUT_MICRO_USD_PER_MILLION = 600_000n / 3_000_000n ($0.60/$3.00 per 1M, groq.com/pricing quoted 2026-07-16). ~5–9× Scout's rate; per-scan token counts are ~2k in / ~150 out, so per-scan cost ≈ $0.0017.
- (Format tolerance — normalization, not laxity) Zod preprocessors normalize ONLY the observed variants: enum strings lowercased (confidence, photo_quality); numeric confidence banded ≥0.75 high / ≥0.4 medium / else low (judgment call, recorded here); non-numeric fill_level → null (unknown, never guessed); container/size_class "none"/"n/a"/"null"/"" → null. Unknown keys and smuggled nutrition fields still fail .strict() — the kcal-smuggling rejection test still passes. The prompt now pins every field format explicitly; live-verified: Qwen returns schema-perfect JSON through the real adapter (pizza fixture, 2026-07-16).

## web repoint — Card 5c: meal composition + synonyms + change-label (2026-07-17)
- (CARD SPLIT, Kd-approved at the plan gate) Card 5c as scoped by cutover.md:122-132 (dishware IN-FLOW + portion API + change-label + stale-guards) was RE-CUT: 5c = meal COMPOSITION (add/remove ingredients) + food synonym aliases + the change-label control + the 5b stale-guard advisories; **dishware IN-FLOW moves to its own card ⑤c2** because driving the server's portion math from a chosen dishware needs a contract design of its own (a new API surface), not a UI tweak. The kickoff prompt asserted this split was already Kd-ruled; the REPO had no such record (S1: the prompt is hearsay), so it was re-confirmed with Kd before coding and is recorded here as the ruling. cutover.md updated accordingly — ⑤c2 is owed, nothing is dropped (NO-REMOVAL).
- (API, Part 2B §3.2 S4) Photo CONFIRM and PREVIEW accept EXTRA items beyond the scan draft (the oats-with-milk case). A chosen item absent from the draft resolves via findFood at portion rung 'default' (the canonical cache from DECISIONS 2026-07-17 makes OFF foods work here too); unresolvable → 400 unknown_food, never a silent drop. ONE shared `resolveDraftItem` serves confirm and preview so live math cannot diverge from what is saved (the standing trust rule). NO schema change: an extra is just another {canonical, grams} entry `chosenItemsSchema` already allows.
- (API, Stage-5 telemetry — T3 finding, CORRECTS the plan's premise) The plan (inherited from the kickoff) claimed the addition "is already recorded as a Stage-5 correction for free" by the originalItems-vs-items diff. That is SEMANTICALLY WRONG and was fixed: an addition is not an estimate error, so folding extras into the diff charged the added item's mass to the rung that estimated the DRAFT items — inflating exactly the signal DECISIONS 2026-07-12 (T3 finding 3) defines ("the rung that produced the corrected-away number"). `MealWrite` gains `correctedItems` = the confirmed values for the ESTIMATED items only. An all-additions confirm leaves originalItems empty and writes NO correction row — `worst([])` falls through every `.some()` and returns the BEST rung ('user_dishware'), i.e. it would fabricate a claim that user-dishware produced an estimate that never existed. Addition-telemetry, if ever wanted, is its own ruled field — not invented here.
- (API, food synonym aliases — the Card-5b roti case) `FOOD_ALIASES` on the curated table: naming metadata only (no nutrition numbers), checked in findCurated BEFORE the fuzzy substring pass and scored in searchCurated; only synonyms the substring match cannot already reach are listed ("biryani"→biryani_chicken already resolves, so it is absent). ~26 entries, each a reviewed judgment call. Plus one MEAL_VISION_PROMPT line nudging canonical_hint toward common local names.
- (API, alias matching — T3 finding, the card did NOT fix its own bug) The first implementation keyed aliases on the WHOLE slugged query, so it only fired on a bare synonym: `findCurated("Flatbread Stack")` → NULL, i.e. the exact input cutover.md:129-132 names was still 0 kcal, while the test asserted `findCurated("flatbread")` — a straw man that passed with the bug live. FIX: a NOISE_WORDS pass strips pure arrangement/quantity/presentation words (stack, plate, slice, of, …) and retries the alias + substring lookup. DELIBERATELY NOT arbitrary token probing: "Aloo Paratha" would then resolve to potato and "Beef Stew" to ground beef, and a WRONG food is worse than an honest "couldn't match" (the Card-5b empty state; Kd's exact-data-only taste). Preparation words like "stew" stay OUT of the noise list for that reason. Verified by command: Flatbread Stack/Roti Stack/Pizza Slice resolve; Aloo Paratha/Beef Stew/Margherita Pizza/Fresh Basil still drop honestly.
- (API, RESIDUAL — recorded, not fixed) Descriptive names whose head noun we DO stock but which the substring pass misses still drop: "Margherita Pizza" → NULL (curated "Pizza (cheese)"), and plurals ("Plate of Rotis") too. Fixing these needs a fuzzier matcher (e.g. head-noun-in-query scoring), which trades false-negatives for false-positives — a product call about honest-drop vs best-guess that is Kd's to make, not a silent widening. The prompt nudge is the first line of defence; the smoke on a real roti photo is what tells us whether it suffices.
- (API, retry-safety — T3 round 2) `confirmMeal` called the destructive `takeDraft` BEFORE resolving items, so one unresolvable ingredient 400'd with the draft already consumed: the scanToken was dead and the only way back was another photo (a fresh Groq call + another 2/day quota unit) to fix a typo. Pre-existing shape, but THIS card made it reachable (before extras, the client could only send canonicals the draft already had). FIX: read the draft non-destructively, resolve everything, `take()` only once nothing can reject — `take()` remains the atomic single-use gate (concurrent confirms both read; only one take() wins). Redis-down still reports 503 not 400: `get()` conflates missing-with-down, so the unreadable-draft path falls through to `take()`, whose Lua GET+DEL distinguishes them.
- (WEB) PhotoModal "+ Add an ingredient" (in-flow, where the mistake is visible — Kd's taste); extras ride the SAME confirm/preview payload as drafted items, priced live by the server. AddMealModal is DUAL MODE: with a `meal` prop it adds an ingredient to a SAVED meal by PATCHing items = existing (resent at stored gramsPoint) + new — the API already accepted any searched food there, so no new endpoint. ## Card 5c2 API — dishware portions (in-flow "measure with my dish") (2026-07-18)
- (DESIGN RULING, Kd — DEVIATION from 2B §3.2 Stage 5) The spec's Stage 5 says a saved dish is auto-applied to every future scan of that container and "the question never repeats". Kd ruled the opposite: **ASK EVERY TIME, never silently auto-apply** — a user may eat from a different bowl each meal, so the saved bowls are offered as tap-to-pick choices at confirm, never a locked default. Consequence that simplifies the build: because the user actively picks their dish (rather than the app detecting + auto-filling it), the analyze/scan RESPONSE SHAPE IS UNCHANGED — no container/fillLevel echo needed, no migration. The web just adds a "measure with my dish" affordance per item.
- (CONTRACT, packages/shared) `chosenItemsSchema` item is now a UNION of two .strict() arms: the grams arm `{canonical, grams}` (unchanged) OR the dishware arm `{canonical, dishwareId(uuid), fillLevel(0<..≤1)}`. Both strict → a hybrid `{canonical,grams,dishwareId}` matches NEITHER and 400s (no ambiguity). Applies uniformly to confirm, preview (both arms), manual, and PATCH — all four already route items through the shared resolvers.
- (SERVER MATH, the can't-disagree guarantee) `dishwareGrams(volumeMl, fillLevel, canonicalHint) = round(volume × fill × density(food))` is EXTRACTED into portion-priors.ts and called by BOTH the scan-time rung-1 resolver AND the confirm-time dishware arm (service.normalizeChosen), so a bowl measured in the photo flow and the same bowl chosen at confirm compute identical grams. Unit-test pins the equality. The dishware arm always stamps rung `user_dishware`; range collapses to a point (user-chosen).
- (TENANCY, R3.2) New `repo.getDishware(sql, userId, id)` is userId-scoped; a foreign/missing dishwareId returns null → service 400s `unknown_dishware`, never resolves another user's dish. Route test proves a stranger's dishwareId 400s (not someone else's grams).
- (JUDGMENT CALL 1, Kd-agreed) `fillLevel` is REQUIRED in the dishware arm (no default). The scan resolver defaults a missing fill to 1, but a user actively measuring must state how full — inventing "full" would fabricate a portion. UI offers ¼/½/¾/full = 0.25/0.5/0.75/1.0; the contract accepts any (0,1].
- (JUDGMENT CALL 2, recorded inference) Confirm-time density keys off the item's `canonical` (e.g. `dal_lentil_curry`) where scan-time keyed off the vision's `canonical_hint` (e.g. `dal`); `density()` substring-matches ("dal"⊂"dal_lentil_curry", "sabzi", "rasam"), so the same class resolves — same normalization family. Recorded rather than assumed silently.
- (PROVE) api 276/276 on Neon (272 + 4 dishware route tests); unit +1 (dishwareGrams==resolver equality); typecheck + lint clean. NO migration, NO response-shape change.
- (T3 F1 — fixed) The dishware arm produced no lower/upper bound on the RESOLVED grams, unlike the grams arm (chosenItemsSchema: positive, ≤10_000). A tiny dish × low fill rounds to 0 g (e.g. 1 ml × 0.25 × thin = 0) → persists a MealItem the shared mealItemSchema declares impossible (gramsPoint.positive) → unrenderable on read; and a large dish × thick could exceed 10_000 g (10000 ml × 1 × 1.1 = 11000), bypassing the grams arm's cap. FIX: normalizeChosen rejects a resolved gram <1 or >10_000 with 400 `portion_out_of_range`, symmetric with the grams schema. Verified by probe (0 and 11000 reproduced) + boundary route tests.
- (T3 F2 — fixed) PATCH /meals/:id had no dishware-arm test (only preview/manual/confirm did). Added: a PATCH that re-measures a saved item with a dishware arm → grams recomputed, rung overridden to user_dishware; plus a foreign-dishwareId-on-PATCH 400 (tenancy holds on the edit path too). api 278/278 on Neon.

## web repoint — Card 5d: previous-days meal view (2026-07-19)
- (SCOPE + APPROACH = option a, per cutover.md:148-150) The Nutrition page showed only today (client-side isToday filter over listMeals(100)); Card 5d adds day navigation (‹ / › / date picker) to look back at earlier days. **NO API change:** GET /v1/nutrition/meals has no date filter (nutritionListQuerySchema is {limit,cursor}, cursor opaque), so `listMealsForDay` page-walks the newest-first list (`walkMealsForDay`, nutritionApi.js) until it passes the target LOCAL day — MEAL_PAGE_SIZE=100, MAX_MEAL_PAGES=10 (~6 months at ~5 meals/day) then an honest "couldn't load back this far" fallback. Option (c) server-side date filter stays the documented upgrade path (cutover.md) if history runs deeper. **T3 verified the linchpin:** the server orders `taken_at DESC, id DESC` (repo.ts:222) matching the `(taken_at,id) < cursor` predicate, and takenAt is user-editable (handleEditTime) — so the newest-first early-stop is correct and no in-day meal hides behind an older row (ordering by created_at would have silently dropped edited-time meals).
- (DROPPED the session page-cache floated at plan-review — deliberate, recorded) Each mutation (delete/rename/relabel/edit-time/add-ingredient) already calls loadData() to refresh, so a cross-navigation cache would need invalidation on every one of those — trading a real stale-after-edit risk for a negligible perf win (adjacent-day nav is 1-2 free DB reads). The simpler always-refetch is the more T3-defensible call. Flagged to Kd since the "is your plan correct" reply had said caching would be folded in.
- (past-day interaction — Kd ruling 2026-07-17 enforced) Logging affordances (hero photo button + section "+") are HIDDEN on past days: a new meal always stamps the real current time, so it would land under today, not the viewed day. Per-meal edits (delete/rename/relabel/edit-time/add-ingredient) STAY on past days (they PATCH/DELETE existing rows). Back-dated logging would need a change to the current-time ruling → possible follow-up, not built.
- (past-day left column) "Remaining today" (target−eaten) is a today concept; on a past day it becomes "Eaten on this day" (that day's totals, no target math). **MacroRings STAYS on past days — Kd RULED KEEP (2026-07-19):** it fills toward today's targets while showing that day's server-summed totals; all numbers real/server-sourced (D3, no fabrication), targets are stable, and no historical targets are stored. T3 flagged the semantics as a conscious product choice; Kd chose keep.
- (day math) All local calendar days (startOfDay/isSameDay/addDays), matching the isToday filter it replaces; date <input> uses local YYYY-MM-DD (toISOString would shift the day west of UTC), parsed back local-only.
- (T3 F1 — stale-response race, fixed) Rapid ‹/› navigation fires overlapping loadData(d) page-walks; a slower earlier response could resolve last and paint the wrong day under the current label. loadData now stamps `latestDayReq` (a ref) with the day it fetches and drops superseded results (and their toast + spinner-ownership). Not unit-expressible without jsdom (web is node-vitest only, R1.4) — SMOKE is its proof.
- (T3 F2 — truncated vs empty honesty, fixed) When the walk hits the page cap before reaching the day (`truncated`), the client CANNOT know the day is empty. Three cases, never asserting unverified emptiness: truncated+nothing → "couldn't load back this far" only (no sections, which would each falsely say "none"); truncated+partial → banner + sections; not-truncated → true empty state or sections. The truncated flag itself is unit-tested (walkMealsForDay cap test).
- (T3 finding — date bar was inside the loading gate, fixed) goToDay's setLoading(true) blanked the whole grid (arrows included) to a spinner on every day change, so rapid ‹‹‹ (the reason F1's guard exists) wasn't reachable through the UI. Restructured: the grid + date bar always render; each column's CONTENT gates on loading. Arrows stay clickable mid-walk.
- (SMOKE-folded meal-row UX fixes — Kd asks 2026-07-19, recorded per the established pattern; MealRow surface built in 5c/5c2, no API change) (1) **RENAME BUG:** the name input's onBlur discarded the edit (setEditingName(false) with no save), so clicking away reverted the name and NO PATCH ever fired — proven by the api log (only GETs during a rename attempt). Fixed: single commit path via onBlur — Enter and click-away both save, Escape flags a cancel (nameCancelRef) so blur skips. Server PATCH already accepts mealName (patchMealRequestSchema, nutrition.ts:101); the bug was purely client. (2) **Discoverability:** an always-visible ✏️ pencil next to each meal name signals it's editable. (3) Row action buttons (relabel/tag · +add-ingredient · delete) no longer hover-gated (opacity-0 group-hover removed) — always visible. JSX-handler changes, not unit-expressible — SMOKE is the proof.
- (PROVE) web 84/85 (the 1 = the known syncClient VITE_API_URL env quirk, passes in CI, DECISIONS 2026-07-15) · vite build ✓ · lint **7 errors / 0 warnings = the Nutrition.jsx 7-error baseline parity** (5 set-state-in-effect + 2 no-unused-vars; the new exhaustive-deps warning from loadData closing over selectedDate is suppressed on the mount-only effect with a rationale comment). New tests: nutritionApi.test.js +5 (walkMealsForDay window/early-stop/cap + listMealsForDay cursor-passthrough).
- (T3 — FRESH CHAT, per CLAUDE.md:129) Kd ran the T3 in a separate fresh chat (not a subagent): ZERO violations, security clean, independently verified the taken_at ordering linchpin. One non-blocking finding (date bar in loading gate) fixed above. **SMOKE PASSED** (Kd 2026-07-19, every step ✅, incl. re-smoke of the meal-row fixes and the loading-layout fix).

## Desktop webcam capture for meal photos — WON'T BUILD (2026-07-19, Kd ruled)
- (THE RULING) The queued "desktop webcam capture" enhancement (cutover.md; DECISIONS 2026-07-17 Card-5b product asks) is **dropped, not deferred**. Kd raised it and ruled after a cited recommendation. NOT a feature removal — grounding confirmed NO meal-photo webcam capture was ever built: `useCamera.js` (getUserMedia) serves ONLY the workout/pose path (ActiveWorkout, PreWorkout), and nothing in the nutrition flow uses it. So the MIGRATION-STANCE no-removal rule is not engaged; this is declining to build a never-built enhancement.
- (spec check) Part 2B §3 specifies the photo PIPELINE (one vision call, portion resolver, photos never stored) and mandates NO capture mechanism — the spec is silent, so this was Kd's call to make (R0.2 respected: nothing invented).
- (no user is blocked) The meal photo input is `<input type="file" accept="image/jpeg,png,webp" capture="environment">` (Nutrition.jsx:1084-1091). `capture` is a hint DESKTOP BROWSERS IGNORE → on a laptop it opens the normal file picker, so a desktop user can already log a meal from any photo on disk. On phones it opens the rear camera directly.
- (the deciding rationale — accuracy, not effort) A laptop webcam is a materially WORSE input to the exact problem 2B §3 exists to solve (monocular portion estimation, "the same dal in a 150 ml katori vs a 400 ml bowl"): fixed, front-facing, low-res, forcing the plate to be held up at an unnatural angle. It would push more scans into the `photo_quality:"poor"` 422 retake path — paying twice (each scan is a paid Groq vision call ~$0.0017 + one of the 2/day free quota slots, DECISIONS 2026-07-16) for a worse answer. Accepted cost of the ruling, stated honestly: a laptop user with food in front of them and no phone to hand cannot capture in the moment; they need a photo already on disk. Judged too thin to build for — the phone is the natural device and the responsive web app already serves it.
- (OWED, UNVERIFIED — raised at the same ruling) DECISIONS 2026-07-17's claim that "the file input already opens the camera on phones (capture attr)" is **NOT device-verified** (V1): every smoke to date (Cards 4, 5a, 5b, 5c, 5c2, 5d) ran on Kd's DESKTOP browser. Since this ruling makes mobile web the PRIMARY meal-capture path, a real-phone smoke is owed — it needs `vite dev --host`, `VITE_API_URL` + the API's `WEB_ORIGIN` pointed at the laptop's LAN address (a phone resolves `localhost` to itself, and CORS is exact-origin + credentials, the Card-4 lesson). Kd deferred the test ("test later"); recorded in cutover.md so it is not lost.
- (a trade-off recorded with it, NO ruling yet) `capture="environment"` sends the user straight to the rear camera (one tap, ideal in-the-moment) but on browsers that honor it strictly it BYPASSES the photo library — a user who photographed lunch 20 minutes ago may have to retake. Options presented: (A) keep as-is · (B) drop `capture` so the phone shows a Take-Photo/Library chooser, taxing every log one tap · (C) two explicit buttons ("Take photo" / "Choose photo"), both one tap and discoverable. RECOMMENDED **A now, C later** — only if the owed phone smoke shows the gallery limitation actually bites. No code changed; A is the current behavior.

## Nutrition targets API — the Mifflin-St Jeor port (2026-07-20)
- (THE GAP, command-verified) `GET /v1/nutrition/targets` did not exist: a grep for `mifflin|bmr|tdee|calorieTarget|dailyTarget` across ALL of `apps/api/src` + `packages/shared/src` returned only prose in a coach knowledge `.md`. The web's MacroRings + "Remaining today" therefore still read the OLD backend via `nutritionApi.js`'s `getTargets` → mlApi — the D2 interim Kd ruled at Card 5a (DECISIONS 2026-07-16), recorded as the owed **"Nutrition targets/remaining (MacroRings + Remaining today)"** checkbox in **web-repoint's** RUNBOOK/cutover.md owed-endpoints list (that list does not exist on master's copy — T3 round 2 caught this as the third instance of the cross-branch citation class). This card is the API half; the web half repoints the page. NO migration — targets are computed per request from stored profile data, never stored.
- (CITATION DISCIPLINE — T3 finding, recorded because the mechanism will recur) The two line numbers this entry originally carried (`nutritionApi.js:210`, `cutover.md:103-116`) were verified on the **web-repoint** branch and written into a **master**-bound commit, where the same files are the pre-repoint versions (47 and 88 lines) and those lines do not exist. Both were real readings of the wrong checkout, which is worse than a guess because they survive a re-read on the author's branch. RULE for every cross-branch card: cite web-repoint file positions by QUOTED TEXT, never by line number, and name the branch when a line number is unavoidable.
- (INPUTS) Five values, spanning two tables: `user_fitness_profiles` (age, gender, height_cm, exercise_frequency, fitness_goals — populated by BOTH the wizard (Card 6) and Settings (Card 7)) + `users.weight_kg`. Read via a new sql-only `getUserTargetContext(sql, userId)` in users/service.ts, mirroring the existing `getUserSyncContext` precedent (:27): the exported `getProfile`/`getFitnessProfile` take `UsersDeps{sql,redis,emailSender,log}` and `NutritionDeps` has no emailSender, so nutrition cannot call them. It composes the two TESTED repo reads (2 indexed PK lookups, once per page load) rather than adding a join, keeping all DB access in repo.ts (R4.6) and adding no new SQL to review.
- (KD RULING 1 — HONEST EMPTY STATE, no fabricated defaults) The salvage defaults every missing input (weight 70 / height 170 / age 25 / gender "male", nutrition.py:103-106) and flags it with `using_defaults` (:178). NOT ported: a fabricated target renders identically to a real one, which is the exact class the Card-7 F2 ruling struck down ("unanswered is not 'beginner'"). The response is `{targets, missing[]}` with `targets: null` EXACTLY when `missing` is non-empty — the client names what to fill in instead of showing a generic 2000.
- (KD RULING 2 — all five inputs REQUIRED) age · gender · heightCm · weightKg · exerciseFrequency. Each moves the number materially (frequency alone swings it ~700 kcal: 1.2 vs 1.9, :140-141). `fitnessGoals` is deliberately NOT required — the salvage has a real no-adjustment branch (:152-153), so an empty goal list is an answer, not an omission.
- (PORT FIDELITY, Part 0 rule 4 / R5.4) Every constant carries its nutrition.py line in `targets.ts`: BMR female −161 (:127) / else +5 (:129); the 7 activity multipliers (:140-141); tdee (:145); goal adjust −400/+300/0 (:148-153); kcal floor 1200 (:155); protein/kg 2.2/2.0/1.6 (:158-163); fat = kcal·0.25/9 (:166); carbs (:167) with its 50 g floor (:174). Goldens in the unit test are hand-computed from these same lines, then pinned.
- (SALVAGE QUIRK, ported deliberately + pinned) The kcal adjustment tests `weight_loss` FIRST (:148-151) while the protein split tests `muscle_gain` FIRST (:158-161). A user with BOTH goals therefore gets the cutting calorie target (−400) AND the bulking protein figure (2.2 g/kg). That inconsistency is in the original; porting it verbatim is what R5.4 requires, and a unit test pins it so no future edit "tidies" it into consistency without a ruling. Kd may open a card to change it — that would be a product decision, not a port fix.
- (gender other / prefer_not_to_say) Both fall to the salvage's `else` (+5, :128-129), i.e. the male formula. Mifflin-St Jeor defines only two formulas; inventing a midpoint would be re-deriving a constant (R0.2). Recorded rather than assumed silently.
- (NOT PORTED, each with a reason) (a) the lbs→kg (:115-118) / ft→cm (:120-123) branches — legacy Mongo stored `{value,unit}` documents; the new API is metric-only, so there is no unit to inspect. (b) `fiber_g` (:176) + `water_ml` (:177) — command-verified that nothing in `apps/web/src` renders a fibre or water target, so they would be dead surface (R1.1). (c) the defaults + `using_defaults` (ruling 1 above).
- (UNREACHABLE BRANCH, recorded) The salvage's `activity_map` string keys — "1-2"/"3-4"/"5-6"/"daily" (:132-137) — can never fire on new data: `user_fitness_profiles.exercise_frequency` is an INTEGER column (identity.ts:132), so only the `freq_map` 1-7 path (:140-141) is live. The ported `.get(frequency, 1.55)` fallback (:143) is KEPT because R5.4 requires porting it verbatim — it is DEFENSIVE ONLY, not currently reachable. Zod is the sole writer of `exercise_frequency` (upsertFitnessProfile ← the PUT's `.min(1).max(7).nullable()`, users.ts:141); migration 0006 declares a bare integer with NO CHECK behind it (the table's only CHECKs are gender / fitness_level / preferred_workout_time), so the fallback earns its keep the day a second writer appears, degrading an out-of-range integer to the ported default instead of NaN (I6). **THIS ENTRY WAS WRONG TWICE, IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS** — round 3 corrected an asserted DB CHECK that does not exist; that correction then asserted "P2.7-migrated rows never pass through Zod at all", also FALSE (T3 round 6): the migrator never writes this table at all — INVENTORY.md:45 drops the onboarding fields and collections/users.ts:80 inserts only `users` columns. Rounds 4 and 5 both re-read the sentence and missed it, because they verified the CHECK half (true) and not the migration half. Adding the CHECK would be its own small migration card, not a silent addition here.
- (ROUNDING) Python `round()` is half-to-even, JS `Math.round` half-up — the measure-zero divergence class already ruled at DECISIONS 2026-07-07. As in the salvage, all arithmetic stays in floats and rounds ONCE at the end; goldens were chosen off exact-.5 boundaries so the two agree.
- (PROVE) 10 unit tests (activity table verbatim · female and male goldens · other/prefer_not_to_say · the opposite-precedence quirk · goal branches + 1200 floor · 50 g carb floor · protein selection · missing-input reporting · resolveTargets withholding) + 1 route test (401 · brand-new user → all five missing · profile-without-weight → only weightKg missing, pinning that the read spans BOTH tables · complete → the same golden end-to-end through real storage · two users never cross). Full api suite **289/289 on Neon** (278 baseline + 11); typecheck + lint clean.
- (CURL DRIVE, before any handover) Register → login → targets (all 5 missing) → PUT profile → targets (only weightKg) → PATCH weight → targets = the 1646 golden → 401 unauthenticated. NB the first drive 404'd on every call: a STALE api process from an earlier session still held port 3000 (`EADDRINUSE` in the new server's log, confirmed via netstat), so the requests were hitting an old build. Not a code fault — recorded because a 404 there looks exactly like a missing route.
