Exactly the duplication R7.2 exists to prevent, and invisible to tests because the two copies coincided. FIX: `REQUIRED_TARGET_INPUTS = missingTargetInputSchema.options` (derived, cannot drift), the three types are imported from `@app/shared` instead of redeclared, and `resolveTargets` returns the shared `NutritionTargetsResponse`. `TargetInputs` stays local — it is the calculator's INPUT and is never serialized. Guard test pins the derivation; a route test now parses BOTH response arms through `nutritionTargetsResponseSchema` (`.strict()`, so an extra key fails rather than being carried silently).

Added to both the value and type re-export lists; service.ts now imports the type through `./schemas.js` like its siblings.

Behaviour was always safe (`?? DEFAULT_ACTIVITY`), but the comment asserted defence-in-depth that isn't there, Comment and the DECISIONS entry both corrected. (Round 6 corrected them AGAIN — the round-3 replacement claim, that P2.7-migrated rows bypass Zod, was itself false; see the UNREACHABLE BRANCH entry above.) Adding the CHECK is its own migration card if ever wanted.
- (T3 F4/F5 — V1/V2, FIXED) Two line citations verified on web-repoint and written into a master-bound commit. See the CITATION DISCIPLINE line in the card entry above — the standing rule is now: quote text, not line numbers, whenever a card's record crosses branches.

That is TRUE OF MASTER's web app, which is the pre-repoint copy — the review ran against this branch's checkout. On **web-repoint** (where the web half lands) `Nutrition.jsx` already calls `nutritionService.getTargets()` as its own request, so no new API surface is owed. The remaining-math question is ALREADY RULED TWICE and must not be re-litigated (CLAUDE.md: re-asking Kd to rule on something DECISIONS already rules on is a protocol failure): **D2** and **D3**, both at **`web-repoint:DECISIONS.md`** under "## web repoint — Card 5a" — D2: "Targets/remaining rings stay on the OLD backend … remaining = the old server's own max(0, target−total) display formula over new server-computed meal sums"; D3: "Client sums SERVER-computed per-meal totals for the day display … display aggregation only". The 2B doctrine bans the BROWSER deriving nutrition (kcal/macros from foods and grams, where a wrong number would be fabricated data); subtracting two server-computed numbers for display is not that. So: NO new API surface and no `remaining` endpoint. Recorded here so the web card inherits the citation instead of rediscovering the question.

This SUPERSEDES `web-repoint:DECISIONS.md`'s Card-5b line "(Remaining-today defaults — Kd smoke finding) … Remaining falls back to the SAME default goals MacroRings renders (2000/150/250/65 …) instead of showing zeros" — approved only while targets were dark for EVERYONE; once real targets exist, the fallback only ever misleads the user with an incomplete profile.

## Nutrition targets API — T3 round 3 (2026-07-20; fresh chat)
- (round-3 verdicts on the round-2 fixes) The reviewer independently re-verified: the refine() rejects both impossible states; the guard test genuinely fails (they shrank the shared enum and watched it go red, then restored); the seam import holds; and all five goldens recompute exactly against nutrition.py:126-174. Security pass clean again (authn, tenancy-by-construction, R3.1, parameterized SQL, no log/secret leak, the contract throw maps to a generic 500 with no internals).
- (F1 — FIXED, the one that mattered) `missingTargetInputs` filtered `input[key] === null`, which caught the enum SHRINKING but not it GROWING: a key added to the shared enum whose `TargetInputs` field is non-nullable (e.g. `fitnessGoals: string[]`) compiles, never equals null, and is therefore silently unenforced — a "required" input that never blocks a target. FIX (as CORRECTED at round 4 — the round-3 version was itself defeatable): the fields are projected through a mapped type asserting NULLABILITY, `satisfies { [K in MissingTargetInput]: K extends keyof TargetInputs ? (null extends TargetInputs[K] ? TargetInputs[K] : never) : never }`, so a new enum key missing from the literal fails the BUILD and one whose field cannot BE null collapses to `never` and also fails.
- (F3 — FIXED) `resolveTargets`'s doc promised "the shared contract's refine() rejects either impossible pairing", but the parse lived only in `service.getTargets` — and `resolveTargets` is exported and directly unit-tested, so every other caller got zero enforcement. The parse now runs INSIDE `resolveTargets` (the service's duplicate removed), so the guarantee is true for all callers. Same class as the round-2 F1 finding: a doc comment asserting an enforcement the artifact did not carry.
- (F2 — FIXED) The narrowing chain's comment called itself "the drift alarm"; it alarms on enum SHRINK only (growth is now caught at the `satisfies`). Reworded to say exactly that.
- (F10 — FIXED) zod 3's `.options` getter returns the schema's OWN internal array, so `REQUIRED_TARGET_INPUTS` was a live mutable alias — a consumer's `.sort()` would reorder the shared contract in place. Probed and confirmed (`same object reference: true`, `frozen: false`). Now `Object.freeze([...options])`, with a test pinning both properties.
